<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/knowledge-memory`, `@objectstack/knowledge-ragflow`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **44** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-ragflow/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/package.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), documentId (symbol, a field of interface AdapterListedDocument))_
- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via nextCursor (symbol, a field of interface AdapterListDocumentsPage))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via IKnowledgeAdapter (symbol, a top-level interface), KnowledgeDocumentSchema (symbol, a top-level const), KnowledgeReindexResult (symbol, a top-level interface), KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), docHash (symbol, a field of interface AdapterListedDocument; a field of interface ChunkRecord), documentId (symbol, a field of interface AdapterListedDocument), indexDocument (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService), listDocuments (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeAdapterContractOptions; a method of class KnowledgeMemoryAdapter; a method of interface IKnowledgeAdapter), makeAdapter (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeAdapterContractOptions), nextCursor (symbol, a field of interface AdapterListDocumentsPage), reindexSource (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService), runKnowledgeAdapterContract (symbol, a top-level function), listDocuments (literal, a string literal in runKnowledgeAdapterContract))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via nextCursor (symbol, a field of interface AdapterListDocumentsPage))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-ragflow/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/package.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **20** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a1b69c0b196ae3785c7c6b8027e80fe774d0165` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `164927445888f8160ba55bff05a7c6a1671a4285` — the merge of head `8ba26077dea4ad94150c04d21ccf32190ee001dc` into base `0a1b69c0b196ae3785c7c6b8027e80fe774d0165`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 164927445888f8160ba55bff05a7c6a1671a4285 && git checkout 164927445888f8160ba55bff05a7c6a1671a4285
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0a1b69c0b196ae3785c7c6b8027e80fe774d0165 8ba26077dea4ad94150c04d21ccf32190ee001dc && git checkout -B drift-repro 0a1b69c0b196ae3785c7c6b8027e80fe774d0165 && git merge --no-ff 8ba26077dea4ad94150c04d21ccf32190ee001dc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a1b69c0b196ae3785c7c6b8027e80fe774d0165
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0a1b69c0b196ae3785c7c6b8027e80fe774d0165` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `58478cafac5ea4348b684bb80ee2a60a9efae38c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-document.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/knowledge-adapter.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/knowledge-service.ts` + `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/testing.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service-plugin.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/package.json`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/tsup.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/__tests__/knowledge-service.test.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/src/__tests__/contract.test.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-ragflow/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `.changeset/37096-knowledge-list-skip-purge.md` + read, not reviewed: `docs/adr/0161-knowledge-platform-boundary-platform-owns-assembly-sync-split-record-return-knowledge-source-is-a-governed-type.md`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-cluster/package.json`, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/**`, `packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-driver.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts`, `.changeset/config.json`

First review of this PR. Inputs read: card #37096 (body and its three comments: triage 7143730265, claim 7147400808, dev report 7148521174), the PR body at this head, the full diff from the merge base `6f3a8da2` (19 files), the files at this head, ADR-0161 K7 and K8 on this tree, and the 75 check-runs on this head (62 success, 12 skipped, 1 cancelled; the cancelled one, `PR-body guards`, has a later success of the same name; `Check Changeset` success twice). The zone's conclusions were not taken as input; each claim below was read in the code.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept sets and published types, each read at this head:

- `IKnowledgeAdapter.listDocuments?(ctx, opts)` (`knowledge-adapter.ts`): an optional method, so every adapter written before it still satisfies the interface. Shape is ADR-0161 K8 item 1 word for word: `{ cursor?, limit }` in, `{ documents: { documentId, docHash? }[], nextCursor? }` out. The three new exported interfaces are in `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json`, and nowhere else is owed (both baselines are name-level; `KnowledgeReindexResult` and `KnowledgeDocument` were already listed).
- `KnowledgeDocument.docHash` (`knowledge-document.zod.ts`): `z.string().optional()` with a `.describe` that says "Service-computed … stored and returned as stored by the adapter". Schema-optional, described as service-set. The object is not strict, so no input that parsed before is refused now.
- `KnowledgeReindexResult.skipped?: number` and `purged?: number | null` (`knowledge-service.ts` in spec): two optional keys on a result type. K8's "What counts as a member" places both outside the member list ("land with their reader under ADR-0049"), and the reader lands here.
- `authorable-surface/ai.json` gains exactly `ai/KnowledgeDocument:docHash`. One key added to the schema, one line added to the shard, in sort order. Matches.

Declared-and-enforced (ADR-0049), for `docHash`:

- Producer: `recordToDocument` stamps it on every document it builds (the walk and the event sync both go through it), and `indexDocument` stamps `computeDocHash(doc)`.
- Refused on write, not replaced: `indexDocument` throws when `doc.docHash !== undefined`, before `adapter.upsert`, and the message names the document, the field and what to do ("docHash is computed by the knowledge service …; omit it"). `requireSource` and `getAdapter` run first, so an unknown source still answers its own error. `indexDocument` is the only door in `packages/` where a caller hands the service a document (no route or tool calls it).
- Readers: `knowledge-memory` stores it per chunk and lists it; `walkObjectSource` compares it. So the key is produced, stored and read in this PR.
- This refusal is not a narrowing: the key did not exist on `main`, so no accepted input is taken away.

`purged?: number | null`:

- `null` means no purge ran. Every return of `reindexSource` sets it explicitly: `null` on the two refusals before the walk, on a bad `limit`, on `dryRun`, on a stopped page, on a `limit` walk, on `refresh.onRecordChange: false`, on an adapter without `listDocuments`, and on a failed listing; a number after a purge, including the count reached before a purge that stopped (`ok: false`).
- Documented in the spec JSDoc, the service JSDoc, the changeset and the protocol doc, and the four texts agree on the rule. See N1 for the two cases the spec JSDoc's list leaves out.
- Consistent with K8 item 1 ("the result says `purged: null`") and rule 2 ("Nothing is skipped silently").

The `./testing` subpath:

- `exports["./testing"]` has an `import` condition only (`types` + `default`), no `require`; the CJS half of `tsup.config.ts` builds `src/index.ts` alone. `vitest` is `external`.
- `src/index.ts` is not in the diff and imports nothing from `testing.ts`; `testing.ts` imports `KnowledgeService` from `./knowledge-service.js`, the other direction. So nothing reachable from `.` imports `vitest`. The built chunk graph was not inspected here (no build run); the zone reports it, and no check-run on this head is red.
- It is the `service-cluster` shape byte for byte (same export block, same `build` script, same split by format). See N4.

Behaviour that moves for an existing caller: over an adapter with `listDocuments`, `indexed` no longer equals `discovered` after an unchanged reindex, and a complete reindex now deletes documents. The only such adapter in the tree is `knowledge-memory`. Adapters without the method take the `listed === undefined` arm, which is the old walk plus two result keys; the thirteen older exact-result assertions gained only `skipped: 0, purged: null`.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes`: right, and present line-initial in the changeset and the PR body. Every spec edit adds an optional member; nothing is removed, retyped or made required.
- `Metadata-protocol: added`: right by the gate's rule. The authorable-surface shard moved by one key, and the zone's note (no metadata author writes `KnowledgeDocument`; the shard lists every exported `ai/` schema) is true to the tree. The claim comment said `none`; the changeset and the body are the governing texts and both say `added`.
- `Skills-docs: none — …`: present in both places, with a reason. It holds: `git grep` over `skills/` at this head for `KnowledgeDocument`, `listDocuments`, `reindexSource`, `docHash` and `indexDocument` finds one line, `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:233`, which names `IKnowledgeAdapter` in passing and teaches none of its members.
- Levels: `@objectstack/spec` minor (a protocol addition takes minor, AGENTS.md), `service-knowledge` and `knowledge-memory` patch. All three sit in the one `fixed` group of `.changeset/config.json`, so they release together at the highest level. `knowledge-ragflow` has no entry and owes none: its only change is a test config.

### ③ Boundary flags

- File surface: the two paths outside the claim (`contracts/knowledge-service.ts`, `knowledge-ragflow/vitest.config.ts`) were asked for in the dev report's `open_questions` and are recorded as granted under Deviations. The first is card What 4 and K8's stated home for the fields. The second is one anchored alias line; no ragflow source moves.
- Both `open_questions` are answered by the head (option A each).
- `out_of_scope_findings`, first entry (the purge's id text): answered as S2 below. Second entry (`knowledge-memory` lists no empty-content document): read and agreed as the safe direction. Such a document has no chunk, so there is nothing to purge and nothing to serve; it is rebuilt each reindex.
- SQL push-down: the walk materialises every listed document id (`Map`) and every seen id (`Set`), and the purge re-reads one row per candidate. A reason is given and it holds: ADR-0161 K1 ("Why the purge and the grouping run in the service, not in SQL") — the index sits behind the adapter contract and may live in another store, so the anti-join cannot be pushed down in general; K8 item 13 keeps the in-store form for a later reader. The per-candidate re-read is what lets each confirm run on that document's sync chain.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- K at this head is 22. Size: 1213 additions, 60 deletions, 19 files.
- No security finding.

### ④ Design judgment

`knowledge-adapter.ts` against ADR-0161 K8 and its first consumer: holds. The service reads the listing once before the walk, treats an entry without a hash as changed, refuses a repeated cursor and a malformed page, and a failed listing costs the skip and the purge but not the walk. `knowledge-memory` implements it in id order with the last id as cursor, and the suite pins 0, one page and one page + 1.

`knowledge-document.zod.ts`: holds, as in ①.

`contracts/knowledge-service.ts`: holds; N1.

The purge against the card's acceptance: candidates are listed-before minus seen; the purge is skipped on `cap !== undefined`, on `dryRun` (returned earlier), on any stopped page (returned earlier), on `onRecordChange: false` and without a listing. Each candidate goes through `rereadRow`, which is the event sync's read lifted out unchanged (`where` AND `{ id }`, `limit: 1`, system context), now called from both places.

S1 (should-fix) — the per-document chain around the purge has no pin. `purgeDocuments` runs each confirm-and-delete through `serialize`, which the service binds to `recordSyncTails`, and the JSDoc, the protocol doc and the PR body all state the guarantee: an event sync of the same row cannot land between the re-read and the delete. Reading the tests, no case holds the purge's re-read open while an event sync of that document arrives. The one race test ("a document written by the event sync during the walk survives the purge") awaits `handleRecordUpsert` to completion before the walk is released, so it passes with `serialize` replaced by a direct call. Without the chain the order re-read (no row) → restore and its sync (upsert) → delete leaves a live row with no document. A case that holds the `limit: 1` find of the purge, fires `handleRecordUpsert` for the restored row, releases, and asserts the document is present closes it.

S2 (should-fix) — the purge's re-read compares the id as text, and that is a real miss on two shipped drivers. Read through:

- The document id is `${source.id}:${String(record.id)}`; the purge recovers `'5'` from `SRC:5` and re-reads `{ id: '5' }`. The event sync re-reads with the typed id it was handed.
- `driver-sql`, `driver-sqlite-wasm`, `driver-turso`: `id` is `table.string('id').primary()`, varchar(255), minted as a nanoid. A row's id reads back as text, so the text compare is exact. No miss.
- `driver-mongodb`: `create` keeps a caller-supplied `id` as given and mints a nanoid only when none is given; `find` hands the filter to MongoDB, which does not equate `'5'` with `5`. `driver-memory`: `create` keeps `data.id` as given; `find` runs through mingo, which does not either. Platform-minted ids are strings on both, so the miss needs a caller-supplied numeric id. `isRecordId` and the walk's `cursor: string | number` both admit one.
- Effect: on those two drivers a numeric-id row that the complete walk did not see but that exists at purge time (restored, or brought back into `where`, after its page was read) is not found by the re-read, and its document is deleted. The restore's own event sync does not save it when it ran before the purge task. The row itself is untouched; the document comes back at the row's next event or the next complete reindex, which no longer lists it and so writes it.
- That is a wrong deletion from a derived index, narrow and self-healing, not a loss of source data. It is also the one place where the purge and the event sync answer the membership question differently, which `rereadRow`'s own note says a shared helper exists to prevent.
- Today the limit is written only in the PR body and the dev report ("noted, not filed", no carrier). Closing it takes one of: the purge's confirm also matches the number the text spells, with a pin on a numeric-id row restored during the walk; or the limit stated in `purgeDocuments`' TSDoc and the protocol doc's purge section, with a follow-up card filed and named there.

Nits:

N1 (nit) — the spec JSDoc on `purged` lists four causes of `null` and leaves out a failed listing and the two refusals before the walk (non-object source, no engine bound). The sentence "`null` when no purge ran" covers them; the list reads as complete and is not. It also does not say what an absent key means (a service implementation that predates the field).

N2 (nit) — `rereadRow` answers `undefined` when `find` returns a non-array, and the walk ends on a non-array page as if it were empty. Before this PR both were harmless. Now an engine answering a non-array gives a "complete" walk of zero rows and a purge whose every confirm reads "no row". The `IDataEngine` contract promises an array and the shipped engine keeps it, so this is a defensive arm pointing the unsafe way, not a reachable defect.

N3 (nit) — `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` says the service computes `docHash` on every document, and does not say `indexDocument` refuses a caller-supplied one; the changeset and the schema note do. The changeset's "the exported `purgeDocuments` function of the service module" is exported from `knowledge-service.ts` and not from the package entry, so it cannot be imported from `@objectstack/service-knowledge`; row 15's reconcile, if it lives in this package, needs nothing more.

N4 (nit) — `./testing` imports `vitest`, which the package lists under `devDependencies` only. A consumer outside this workspace on a strict installer resolves `vitest` from the package's own tree and may not find it. `service-cluster` and `metadata-core` ship the same shape; an optional peer dependency would state it. Accepted as the precedent's deviation.

N5 (nit) — the skip keys on content, title and metadata. A change of embedder or split leaves every `docHash` equal, so a reindex over a listing adapter rewrites nothing. ADR-0161 K7 answers that with the index fingerprint and generations (K8 item 8), which land with #37099 or #37100; `knowledge-memory` is deterministic and in-process, so nothing is wrong at this head. The first persistent adapter to implement `listDocuments` should not land ahead of item 8.

Tests that pin the new behaviour, read for ablation:

- `indexDocument` refusal: one case asserts the throw by message and `upsert` not called. Removing the refusal turns it red.
- Skip: exact results (`indexed: 0, skipped: 150`) and `upsert` not called; removing the filter turns five cases red, and one in the contract suite.
- Purge confirm: the exact re-read `where`s are asserted, and the restored-row case asserts no delete; removing `rereadRow` turns three red.
- No purge under `limit`, `limit: 0`, `dryRun`, a failed page, `onRecordChange: false`, a failed listing, a repeated cursor: each asserts `purged: null` and no delete.
- A failed re-read: `ok: false`, `purged: 0`, the document kept. Foreign ids: kept, counted in `message`.
- Not pinned: the chain (S1) and a numeric id (S2).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37096-knowledge-list-purge`
Reviewed-by: `fresh subagent of session_01QSeKYpEsWWE9Y5YtSsDgqZ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · L1 · head `58478cafac5ea4348b684bb80ee2a60a9efae38c` · 2026-11-25T02:50Z

- **Shape:** open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #37096`. Every card What item (1–7) and every Acceptance line maps to code and a test, so `Fixes` is right. No closing keyword sits next to another card. Nothing under `content/docs/releases/`. 19 files, +1213/−60, not governed (`check-governed-merges.mjs`).
- **Changeset per published package:** spec `minor`, service-knowledge `patch`, knowledge-memory `patch`. l1-face flags `@objectstack/knowledge-ragflow`. That is a false positive: its only change is `vitest.config.ts`, and its `files[]` ships only `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Premises measured on merge base `6f3a8da2ac`:** no `listDocuments`, no `docHash`, no purge. Both blockers are ancestors. The shapes match ADR-0161 K8 items 1–2 word for word, and ruling 7145942375 (items 1–2) agrees with the skip and the purge.
- **Reindex logic, read:**
  - Skip (`knowledge-service.ts:384-402`) only refrains from writes, so it can never write stale data.
  - The purge gate (`:420-422`) excludes `limit` (`limit: 0` included), `dryRun`, a failed listing and `onRecordChange: false`. Every failure inside the walk returns through `stopped()` with `purged: null`.
  - Candidates are the listed documents minus every document the walk built, skipped ones included.
  - The re-read is extracted unchanged into `rereadRow` (`:960-972`), shared with the event sync.
  - Each confirm-and-delete runs on the event sync's per-document chain, under the same key (`:431` / `:579`). It cannot deadlock against the reindex chain.
- **Memory `listDocuments` (`knowledge-memory/src/index.ts:65-86`):** ids in sorted order, cursor exclusive. `nextCursor` appears only when ids remain, so 0, exactly `limit` and `limit + 1` documents give 1, 1 and 2 pages with no trailing empty page. A non-integer or `< 1` limit is refused. Edges are correct.
- **Tests that go red on revert, by reading:**
  - Skip off: `knowledge-service.test.ts:893/903/914` and contract `testing.ts:271`.
  - Purge or re-read off: `:937/:991/:1048`.
  - Limit or dryRun gate off: `:959`. Failed page made a `break`: `:974`. `onRecordChange` clause off: `:1014`. `indexDocument` refusal off: `:94`.
  - The `:991` double reads at call time, so r001 is a real candidate that only the re-read keeps.
- **Gate check-runs at head:** 75 runs, 62 success, 12 skipped (all expected), 1 cancelled, 0 failed, 0 pending. The cancelled run is `PR-body guards`; a second run of the same name at the same head succeeded, so it needs no action. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` both succeeded, as did `Check Changeset`, Test Core 10/10, Test UI 16/16, every Type Check job and Build Core. Dogfood is not owed.
- **K and staleness:**
  - K from the merge base is 22 (`6f3a8da2..3b4f0b98`). The landing K on PRBASE `a10345abff` is 3, under the hold of 15.
  - No main commit since the merge base touches the PR's 19 files, and `merge-tree` is clean.
  - The PR carries `merge=os-regen` paths (api-surface, export-origins, authorable-surface, references), so section A applies at arming.
- **Accepted deviations, to record at ACCEPT:**
  - The file surface grew by `packages/spec/src/contracts/knowledge-service.ts` (two optional result fields) and `packages/plugins/knowledge-ragflow/vitest.config.ts` (one alias line), exactly as described. The grant is on neither the card nor the PR, so this comment records it.
  - Claim `Metadata-protocol: none` became `added`. The reason is in § Acceptance notes, and `Check Changeset` succeeded.
  - The local `pnpm test` was scoped to the touched packages. CI at head covers the full set.
- **Declarations and docs:**
  - `Clause-②: yes` is correct (contract path and claim), so an L2 contract-tier PASS at head is owed before ready.
  - The `Skills-docs:` line is true: `skills/**` never names `KnowledgeDocument`, `listDocuments`, `docHash` or `reindexSource`, and `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:229-262` teaches `KnowledgeSource` only.
  - `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` is accurate sentence by sentence, apart from the complete-walk sentence, which S1 makes true.
- S1 (should-fix) — `knowledge-service.ts:376` reads a non-array page as the end of the walk, and that now arms the purge. On page 1 every listed document becomes a candidate, and `rereadRow` (`:971`) reads a non-array as "no row", so every candidate is deleted. Send a non-array page through `stopped(...)`, make a non-array re-read throw so the purge stops with `ok: false`, and add a case with a listing adapter for each.
- S2 (should-fix) — No test pins the serialization of the purge's re-read and delete against an event sync of the same document. `serialize: (id, task) => task()` stays green, yet the PR body and `knowledge.mdx` state the property.
